documents.title: Live Eval - Clean Architecture Boundaries
documents.content: Clean Architecture in Cortex separates presentation adapters, application use cases, domain entities, and infrastructure providers. The key rule is that dependencies point inward. Presentation maps HTTP input into DTOs, application use cases orchestrate work, domain objects hold business invariants, and infrastructure implements ports. Tests should verify boundaries without importing framework details into the domain.

documents.title: Live Eval - Celery Composition Root
documents.content: Celery workers act as a second composition root. Worker task files should remain thin adapters. The actual construction of use cases, repositories, cache clients, status cache, task dispatchers, and AI providers belongs in infrastructure celery composition. This keeps task modules small and makes lifecycle cleanup explicit.

documents.title: Live Eval - Scoped Retrieval
documents.content: Scoped retrieval means chat and search must only retrieve chunks from the selected collection. The query payload carries collection_id into the retrieval service, and the database query filters documents by that collection. This prevents unrelated documents from degrading RAG quality as the database grows.

documents.title: Live Eval - Chunk Quality Filters
documents.content: Chunk quality filters reject low-value chunks before answer generation. Empty text, hello text, lorem ipsum, tiny samples, duplicate placeholders, and very short chunks should not enter the final context. This protects source grounding and makes retrieval scores more stable.

documents.title: Live Eval - Production Validation
documents.content: Production retrieval validation runs after deploy against the live API. It seeds temporary collections, uploads text documents, waits until documents are ready, runs scoped query cases, measures source recall, verifies noise rejection, checks abstention cases, writes a JSON report, and deletes temporary seed data.

documents.title: Live Eval - Observability Metrics
documents.content: Operational dashboards should show query latency, retrieval hit rate, failed document processing count, estimated OpenAI cost, and queue depth. Query logs include trace_id, collection_id, source count, used source count, and latency.

documents.title: Live Eval - Refresh Token Revocation
documents.content: Logout revokes the current refresh token by deleting its Redis refresh key. Logout everywhere revokes all refresh tokens for the current user by deleting refresh keys whose value matches the user id. The browser session is then cleared and the refresh cookie is removed.
